title: QBR - NovusMart Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability (99/95p latency), and roadmap alignment for NovusMart's recommender and support automation workloads. Customer is on Hosted + small Dedicated pool; they are evaluating expanding Dedicated capacity for Q4 and want a clearer cost/latency tradeoff. Action items include sharing a detailed per-route cost/latency report, running a 99th percentile latency bench on Dedicated, and drafting renewal pricing scenarios.
next_steps: Avery to send per-route usage + cost breakdown and latency heatmap
Elena to run 99th percentile latency benchmark on their Dedicated pool and share results
Samir to prepare renewal pricing with Dedicated expansion scenarios
Priya/Derek to share projected Q4 traffic and list of critical endpoints
Schedule follow-up demo of batching/kv-cache improvements (week of Aug 31)
action_items: Avery Mitchell: Share detailed usage + cost breakdown and per-route latency (due 2026-08-24)
Elena Ruiz: Run 99th percentile latency bench on Dedicated cluster and share results (due 2026-08-28)
Samir Patel: Draft renewal pricing options and Dedicated expansion tiers (due 2026-09-01)
Priya Shah: Provide Q4 traffic forecast and critical endpoints list (due 2026-08-26)
Derek Lo: Confirm networking constraints for Private/VPC option (due 2026-08-27)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Mitchell (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Martin King (NovusMart Head of ML), Priya Shah (NovusMart VP Eng), Derek Lo (NovusMart Infra), Sofia Nguyen (NovusMart DevOps)

Summary (auto): QBR focusing on usage/cost, reliability, and plan for Dedicated expansion. Next steps agreed at end.

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Happy QBR 
we wanted to walk through last quarter's usage, costs, and reliability, and then sync on your Q4 capacity plans. Martin, Priya, do you want to kick off with any high-level context?
[00:18] Martin: Yeah hi, thanks. Overall thing's looking good, adoption up 24% month over month on the recommender. Support automation is steady. We're mostly concerned with spikes 
the Black Friday-ish test last month showed p99 tails that impacted CI.
[00:35] Priya: And the finance team flagged the token cost for embeddings calls, it's creeping up. We're evaluating whether moving more to Dedicated for steady workloads makes sense, but we need hard numbers.
[00:50] Avery: Totally. We'll show per-route cost and a cost/latency tradeoff for Hosted vs Dedicated. Elena, I'll hand to you for the reliability breakdown.
[01:02] Elena: Cool. So looking at the last 90 days 
p95 for the recommender is ~120ms on Hosted, p99 around 730ms during high concurrency windows. We see most of the tail correlated with cold KV cache misses and bursty sequences. We did a config change in June that improved batching but not enough for peak bursts.
[01:30] Derek: Sorry, when you say KV cache misses, is that the prefix cache? We had some confusions on our side about how cache invalidation works with our deployment.
[01:39] Elena: Right, that's the KV/prefix cache 
we noticed your session keys are low TTL so invalidation gets frequent. Increasing prefix cache TTL where safe reduces backend calls. Also elastic batching helps.
[01:50] Martin: The problem is, for privacy we rotate keys more often, so TTLs can't be too long. Any suggestions?
[02:01] Elena: Understood. Two things 
one, we can recommend partial caching for non-sensitive prefixes, and two, the Dedicated pool gives you better control over KV locality which reduces tail latency. There was a small transcription glitch earlier in our notes where Redwood Dedicated got called Redwood Delicate, ignore that, haha.
[02:18] Priya: (laughs) noted. So on cost 
can you quantify the cost delta for Dedicated expansion? We have baseline committed vs burst pricing questions.
[02:28] Samir: Yeah, I'll cover that. Right now you're on Hosted for spikes and a 4-GPU Dedicated reserve for steady throughput. We estimated committed Dedicated reduces per-token cost by ~28% for your request mix (recommender + embeddings) if utilization stays above ~60%. But it requires a commitment; we'll draft scenarios.
[02:48] Martin: 28% is meaningful. But we need to see the impact on p99 
if Dedicated reduces tail by half, that's worth it.
[02:56] Elena: In our internal tests with similar mix, Dedicated reduced p99 from ~700ms to ~320ms after tuning batching and kernel selection. But results vary with sequence lengths and KV cache behavior.
[03:14] Priya: Can you run a bench on our Dedicated instance? We want the same model, same seq lengths, and our tokenization.
[03:21] Elena: Yes, we can spin up a bench. I'll need a test corpus and traffic profile. Derek, can you share a sample replay or a small traffic dump?
[03:30] Derek: Yeah we can do that 
I need to check privacy filters but we can anonymize.
[03:35] Sofia: One related ask 
our security team wants to confirm KMS integration and audit logs if we expand Dedicated or move to Private. We need SOC 2 attestation details.
[03:46] Avery: Good point. We'll share the SOC 2 report and the KMS integration guide. Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and rotation logs are in the audit trail. We'll attach docs after the call.
[03:58] Priya: Also SSO 
SSAML is working but role-based access needs tightening; Samir, can you help?
[04:06] Samir: Absolutely, we can run an RBAC walkthrough and show best practices for environment separation between Hosted/Dedicated.
[04:14] Martin: On the roadmap front, are there any upcoming features to help with token-level cost visibility? The console is good but we need per-route tokenized breakdowns for product managers.
[04:25] Avery: We're rolling out per-route token-level cost segmentation in the Console in Q4, plus a latent trace integration to map tokens to downstream latency. We'll share the roadmap doc 
tentative dates though.
[04:38] Elena: Also, Redwood Optimize is getting an auto-quantization suggestion tool that recommends quantization / batching profiles per model to reduce cost with minimal quality loss; it's in early access. Might be relevant for embeddings-heavy calls.
[04:53] Martin: That could help. How stable is the auto-suggest? We had a bad quantization experiment last year that regressed accuracy.
[05:00] Elena: Understandable. The tool runs A/B evals on held-out prompts and only suggests when quality delta is within a safe threshold. We'll include a checkpointed rollout plan if you want to try it.
[05:12] Priya: Back to billing 
can you explain the sudden jump in embedding costs last month? The graph shows a spike on July 22.
[05:20] Samir: Looking at the traces, the spike coincided with a batch job that accidentally reprocessed a large historic dataset 
an ETL bug. We gave you a one-time credit for that and proposed a guardrail: limit rate for large batch embeddings jobs and a separate billing tag.
[05:35] Priya: OK good. We'll set a permission for that job so only a few infra users can run it.
[05:41] Derek: Quick question on Private/VPC 
if we go Private later, how seamless is model version pinning and rollout? We don't want a ton of config drift.
[05:50] Elena: The deployment abstraction is the same across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies in the same console; we push an orchestration manifest. A few network steps for VPC peering but we have a runbook.
[06:02] Martin: Any known gotchas around sequence length distribution? Our recommender has long sequences for context and shorter support queries.
[06:10] Elena: Yes the kernel selection and memory layout changes with long sequences; you should consider two model variants or dynamic batching 
Keep a 'long' and a 'short' variant to avoid worst-case kernel selection for short queries. That reduces cost and latency.
[06:28] Priya: Good to know. Can you provide recommended config?
[06:31] Elena: We'll send a config template 
batch settings, kv-cache TTL suggestions, and a policy for routing long vs short.
[06:40] Martin: On actionables, we want the bench results and cost breakdown, then we'll decide on Dedicated expansion by Sept 7.
[06:48] Avery: Perfect. We'll aim for that. Any other items?
[06:52] Sofia: One small items 
can you include an audit of which endpoints are using embeddings the most? That helps us prioritize optimization.
[06:59] Samir: We can add that to the usage report.
[07:03] Priya: Also a ask from finance 
show projected monthly spend under three scenarios: do nothing, expand Dedicated, move 60% of embeddings to a batched offline job.
[07:13] Avery: We'll model those scenarios and include them in the report.
[07:18] Martin: Great. Thanks for the clear plan.
[07:21] Avery: OK recap 
Avery to send usage/cost + per-route tokens & latency heatmap; Elena to run Dedicated p99 bench; Samir to draft renewal pricing; Priya/Derek to send traffic forecast; schedule a follow-up demo of batching and kv-cache optimizations week of Aug 31.
[07:36] Priya: Thanks, everyone. Bye.
[07:39] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels, a few words auto-transcribed ('Redwood Delicate' instead of 'Dedicated'), some punctuation gaps.
